title: Salmon-pink reds
symptom: Reds and skin came out pink/salmon
cause: AgX tone mapping desaturates and hue-shifts saturated reds
fix: Use ACES filmic
rule: Tone-map with ACES (makeRenderer default); never switch to AgX for the cartoon palette

title: Cheap glow look
symptom: Everything bloomed and looked like a screensaver
cause: Bloom/emissive used as a substitute for lighting
fix: bloom: 0 by default; light the scene instead
rule: No glow by default: makePost bloom 0, no glowMat/halo unless the user asks

title: Hard particle squares
symptom: Dust/bubbles rendered as hard squares or diamonds
cause: Default PointsMaterial without a soft sprite
fix: Soft radial falloff in the point shader
rule: Particles always soft round sprites (kit/fx.js particles)

title: Hand-tuned arms miss props
symptom: Hands floated beside cups/flasks, props at the forehead
cause: Arm angles tuned by eye from one camera angle
fix: toon.reach(side, gripPoint) IK
rule: Place the prop first, then reach() to it; check every pose from 3+ angles

title: Feet slide while walking
symptom: Character glides; feet skate on the floor
cause: walk() cycle runs on time, not on distance travelled
fix: Drive walk phase from distance: phase = distance / stride
rule: Walk phase must come from distance covered (stride ~0.7 m), never from t alone

title: Camera passes through a character
symptom: Frame filled with the inside of a head/body for a few frames
cause: Camera path drawn without checking cast positions
fix: Move the character aside or re-route the rail; stills at every key
rule: Render a still at every camera key and midpoint; nothing may intersect the lens

history.note: GSK: camera pushed through detective (case office) and officer (swab); 9:16 framing

title: Black void before a portal
symptom: About 1 s of black between two sets
cause: Camera turned away from the lit subject before the portal filled the frame
fix: Keep the subject lit and in frame until the portal covers it; pass through an object instead of turning away
rule: Camera looks along its path at a lit subject until the portal fill is complete

title: Portal fill held too long
symptom: Solid-colour fill read as a frozen/broken video
cause: Portal half-width too large
fix: Full coverage 4-12 frames (halfWidth 0.15-0.3 s)
rule: Portal full-cover lasts 4-12 frames, never longer

title: Text overflows 9:16
symptom: Signs/wall text cut off at the frame edge
cause: Single long line designed for 16:9
fix: Two short lines; check against 9:16 safe area
rule: All in-world text and captions fit the 9:16 safe area (2 lines max, 1-3 caption words)

title: Unreadable sign lettering
symptom: Embossed/printed text vanished under flat light
cause: Light frontal to the text surface
fix: Raking key light across the text
rule: Light text and screens with a raking key so lettering reads

title: Long render killed by restart
symptom: Hours lost when the container restarted mid-render
cause: Single long process with no resume
fix: Render in 10 s chunks with --from/--to, skip finished chunks, concat
rule: Render in resumable chunks; never one multi-hour process

title: Wrong pixel format
symptom: Output tagged yuvj420p (full range), washed-out on phones
cause: Encoder input range not normalised
fix: Force yuv420p tv range on final encode
rule: Final file is yuv420p, verify with ffprobe

title: Flat plastic materials (mediocre run)
symptom: Everything looked like default MeshStandardMaterial plastic; no surface detail
cause: Single-colour materials with uniform roughness, no normal/roughness maps
fix: Procedural PBR surface sets: albedo variation + normal + roughness maps; world-scale UVs
rule: Every hero surface has albedo variation, a normal map and a roughness map; no bare one-colour materials on hero props

title: Sparse sets (mediocre run)
symptom: Large empty floors and walls; frame looked unfinished
cause: Sets built from a few primitives with no dressing
fix: Instanced clutter, foreground props, background layers, practical lights
rule: Every frame has foreground, midground subject and dressed background; review.py "empty" flags must be zero
where: kit/props.js cozyRoom/lab/street presets + review.py empty check

title: Flat lighting (mediocre run)
symptom: Subjects lit evenly, no depth or mood
cause: Only HDRI/ambient light
fix: Three-point subject rig + motivated practicals (lamps, screens, windows) + rim light
rule: Key + rim on every character, at least one motivated practical per set; review.py "flat" flags must be zero

title: No storyboard to approve (mediocre run)
symptom: The user only saw the result at the end; composition was not planned panel by panel
cause: Went from treatment table straight to the full render
fix: Render a numbered storyboard sheet (stills + timing + narration + camera notes) and get approval before the full render
rule: Always produce and show a polished storyboard sheet before the full render; follow a user storyboard panel by panel when given

title: Mediocre overall result
symptom: User judged the video mediocre
cause: No quality bar, no self-review against previous work
fix: Score every area after each run; the bar ratchets up; weakest area gets effort first next time
rule: Every run must beat the last run in its weakest area and fall below the bar in none

title: Brutalist theme too harsh to watch
symptom: Heavy brutalist sets pulled focus; viewer could not focus on the visuals
cause: Style chosen for mood, not readability
fix: Default style is polished rounded 3D cartoon (look.js/toon.js/props.js)
rule: Default to the polished 3D cartoon look; brutalist only if the user asks
where: SKILL.md default style + kit/look.js, toon.js, props.js

title: Faces must carry emotion
symptom: Faces were simple dots and curves; no emotion on eyes, nose or mouth
cause: Primitive cartoon head with swap-in mouths
fix: Sculpted head + eyes with irises and lids + brows + lips/teeth/tongue + 14 blended emotions + lip-sync
rule: Every line gets a matching emotion on the face (eyes, brows, mouth) plus posture; characters lip-sync when speaking
where: kit/toon.js v3 face rig, EMOTIONS, speech()

title: Coat sized for old body
symptom: Lab coat poked above the shoulders like a tall cylinder after body change
cause: Clothing profiles hard-coded to old proportions
fix: Refit coat profile to the new torso
rule: After any body change, render every outfit (coat, tie, glasses) and check it fits

title: Too many shadow-casting lights
symptom: Shader error: texture image units exceed 32; materials fail to compile
cause: Every house window in street() created a shadow-casting spot light (about 40)
fix: windowFrame only adds a light when intensity > 0; shadow optional
rule: At most ~6 shadow-casting lights per scene; decorative emitters never cast shadows

title: Characters fall outside the 9:16 frame
symptom: Detectives at a desk were cut off; only the laptop was visible
cause: Portrait frame is only ~0.9 m wide at 2.3 m; characters were spaced like a 16:9 shot
fix: Group characters within 0.35 x distance; put them behind the desk facing the camera
rule: Check every two-shot still in 9:16: all faces must be inside the frame with headroom

title: Ground mesh buried the set
symptom: Hill rose 3 m and hid the trunk and root portraits
cause: Scaled sphere placed without computing its top height
fix: Place ground domes so their top sits at y = 0
rule: After building a set, render a wide still of the whole set before choreographing

title: Prop the same colour as its background
symptom: Tambourine skin vanished against a cream door
cause: Prop and background shared a hue and value
fix: Contrasting colour plus a painted design
rule: Hero props must contrast in value or hue with what is behind them

title: Storyboard page with one panel
symptom: Page 3 held a single panel
cause: Fixed 12 panels per page
fix: storyboard.py balances panels evenly across pages
rule: Storyboard pages are balanced

title: No script given
symptom: Only audio was provided; the skill told me to ask for the script
cause: No offline transcription step
fix: scripts/transcribe.py (sherpa-onnx Whisper from GitHub) plus number spelling for the aligner
rule: Transcribe the audio yourself; ask only if that fails

title: Cut detector false positives
symptom: review.py flagged fast pans past saturated props as hard cuts
cause: Colour-histogram jump at 4 fps cannot tell a pan from a cut
fix: Spike test at 15 fps: a cut is one frame far larger than its neighbours
rule: Verify every flagged cut by looking at the frames before acting

title: Camera snaps at move handoffs
symptom: Small visible jumps at 3.8, 7.7, 13.9 and 27.7 s
cause: Piecewise camera moves where the next move's start aim or position differed from the previous move's end
fix: Every move starts from the previous move's exact end (pos, at, fov), or use cameraRail through keys
rule: Write camera moves as a chain: each segment's start = previous end; prefer cameraRail; review.py cut flags at segment boundaries mean a mismatch

title: Whip pan through empty space
symptom: A 0.4 s pan crossed a bare wall corner and read as a cut plus an empty frame
cause: Pan too fast and the route crossed an undressed corner
fix: Slower pan (1.5 s+) and dress everything the pan crosses
rule: Pans last at least 1.5 s and everything they cross is dressed

title: Strobing police lights
symptom: Hard red/blue switching read as cuts and is uncomfortable to watch
cause: Binary on/off flashing
fix: Smooth sinusoidal alternation, never full-frame strobing
rule: No hard strobes: flashing lights fade smoothly (photosensitivity)

title: Viewer cannot follow the story from the visuals
symptom: Audio alone was clear; with the video the viewer lost the context and could not tell what was happening
cause: Shots were decorative metaphors and fast flythroughs; too many environments and portals; key facts never appeared on screen; one idea was not held long enough
fix: Comprehension-first storyboard: every shot literally shows the subject of its sentence, one idea per shot held >= 2.5 s, key facts as on-screen titles, recurring visual anchors, fewer and slower moves
rule: Mute test: with captions hidden, each storyboard panel must still say what the viewer learns; write that takeaway in the treatment and on screen

title: Camera enters doors and objects
symptom: The camera visibly passed into doors, windows and props
cause: Portal moves flew into geometry; no clearance check against props
fix: Keep the lens >= 0.3 m from every surface; portals are colour fills before contact; automatic lens probe in QA
rule: The camera never touches or enters geometry; QA lens probe must report zero hits

title: Hand movement inconsistent
symptom: Hands jumped between poses and elbows flipped
cause: Gestures switched on/off with if-blocks; IK pole given in world space, so elbows flipped when characters turned
fix: Pole vector in the character's local space; every gesture uses smooth envelopes (fade in/out, never a hard start)
rule: No gesture starts or stops abruptly: always env() ramps of >= 0.3 s; check hands every 0.2 s around gesture changes

title: Characters clip into tables
symptom: Hands and bodies passed through desks and tables
cause: Characters placed without checking reach distance to furniture
fix: Stand characters 0.3-0.4 m from furniture edges; hands rest on top surfaces at the measured height
rule: Render a still at every contact (hand on table, prop pick-up) from the side to check for intersections

title: Facial emotions cringy
symptom: Expressions were exaggerated and theatrical; the villain was not menacing, normal people were not natural
cause: Emotion presets at full strength for everyone; villain designed like everyone else
fix: Acting intensity default 0.6; villains get a menacing preset, hood, low key light and red rim; normal people use subtle neutral-to-mild expressions
rule: Normal people: subtle, natural expressions. Villains look evil by design (silhouette, hood, shadowed eyes, under-light), not by grimaces

title: Hand floats beside a held prop
symptom: Officer's fist hovered 7-10 cm from the swab it was meant to hold
cause: IK target offset from the grip point, and the target beyond arm reach (arm 0.56 m)
fix: Aim the wrist at grip point + (0, 0.07, 0) and stand the character within 0.45 m of what the hand touches
rule: Every hand-prop contact: target = grip point + palm offset; check reach distance < 0.5 m; verify in a close still

title: Example still names
symptom: Stills script failed for times like 9.0
cause: render.mjs names files with JS number formatting (9 not 9.0)
fix: Format times the way JS prints them
rule: Use js-style number formatting for still file names

title: Reference look: realistic night-office lighting
symptom: User showed a reference reel that looks realistic through lighting, reflections and soft shadows; our renders look flat and high-key
cause: High-key mood lighting, AO off, hard PCF shadows, wide lenses, weak DoF, oversaturated grade
fix: Low-key practical lighting (lamp key, screen fill, window rim, warm bounce), VSM soft shadows, GTAO, long lenses with strong DoF, glossy hero reflector, sat 1.0 (see references/reference-look.md)
rule: Light every set from motivated practicals in a low-key scene; soft contact shadows and AO always on; long lens plus DoF on character shots

title: Copied the reference's character design
symptom: When asked to match the reference's lighting/environment, the test recreated the reference's man (grey curly hair, round glasses, toy proportions)
cause: Treated the reference as a full style to copy instead of a lighting/environment reference
fix: Take only what the user names (lighting, shadows, reflections, environment); keep the user's own original characters
rule: A reference video is for the aspects the user names only; never recreate its characters or designs

title: Hands with fingers look bad
symptom: Our 3-finger hands look odd; the reference's simple faceted mitten hands look good
cause: Finger detail at cartoon scale reads as creepy
fix: Cute rounded mitten hands (no fingers or nails) by default
rule: Default hands: rounded mittens with a thumb bump, no fingers or nails

title: Too dark and glassy toy look
symptom: Night test was so dark the character could not be seen; glossy materials looked like a glass toy, not a character who acts
cause: Copied the reference's night mood instead of its lighting quality; coat/gloss pushed too high
fix: Bright, readable daylight with soft shadows; satin materials (roughness 0.4-0.6, light coat); character design that can act (real eyes, a pose)
rule: The subject is always clearly lit and readable; reflections are subtle satin, never glass; characters look like actors, not figurines

title: Flat ring-light look, no cast shadows
symptom: Even, frontal daylight looked like an influencer ring light: washed colours, no visible shadows of the table or the person, hands blending into the background
cause: Several big soft fills from the front, a high ambient level, a low-contrast grade, pastel palette
fix: One strong motivated key (sunbeam/lamp) from the side with visible cast shadows, a weak cool fill, low ambient, a saturated complementary palette (teal room vs warm character), a punchy grade
rule: Every shot needs a visible cast shadow from the subject and a clear light direction; colours saturated and separated from the background
